raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Adds `EncDecMultiModalProcessor.process_text_only_encoder_prompt`, which lets encoder-decoder models whose encoder reads the prompt tokens (T5-style text encoders) accept text-only prompts with vLLM's own renderer, and lists the [vllm-t5gemma2-plugin](https://github.com/Chen-afk-art/vllm-t5gemma2-plugin) for T5Gemma 2 in the docs.

Following the review, the Model Runner V2 and `CrossAttention` changes of the first version moved into the plugin, which now runs on unmodified vLLM. This PR keeps only the processor-side hook, for the discussion with @DarkLight1337 below.

## Claims

- **`EncDecMultiModalProcessor.process_text_only_encoder_prompt`** (default `False`): when a processor sets it, the renderer sends encoder prompts without multimodal data through the processor too, so the processor can turn the prompt into the encoder item.
- **Without it**, such a plugin has to register its own renderer and copy `BaseRenderer._process_enc_dec(_async)`, as [the plugin does today](https://github.com/Chen-afk-art/vllm-t5gemma2-plugin/blob/use-vllm-extension-points/vllm_t5gemma2/renderer.py). The flag removes that copy, which would break when the renderer changes. Alternatively, bart-plugin asks users to pass the encoder text as `multi_modal_data`.
- **Docs**: list the T5Gemma 2 plugin, and document the flag for plugin authors.
- **No change for in-tree models**: the flag defaults to the current behavior.

## Validation

| Check | Setup | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `pre-commit run --hook-stage manual` | changed files | passed |
| `pytest tests/renderers` | CPU | 686 passed, 4 failed. The same 4 fail on `main` (`349b214`) in the same environment: three need gated checkpoints (Llama 3.2, PaliGemma), and `test_cohere.py::test_async_cohere_renderer_does_not_block_event_loop` also failed there before. |
| Plugin tests, plugin's own renderer, unmodified vLLM | CPU, vLLM 0.33.0 and `main` (`a91a1d0`), tiny random checkpoint | 5 passed |
| Same, with the plugin's renderer not selected | CPU, `main` (`a91a1d0`) | text-only generation fails: vLLM `[73, 73, …]` vs HF `[59, 59, 85, …]`, since the encoder gets no input |
| Same, renderer not selected, with this flag | CPU, `a91a1d0` + this change | 5 passed |

The plugin tests compare greedy generation with HF transformers token by token (text, one and two images, explicit decoder prompts), LoRA with HF + PEFT, and check text-only mode.

**CI**: no in-tree model sets the flag, so vLLM CI covers its default (existing renderer tests). The new path is exercised by the plugin's tests above.

**Model evaluation**: not applicable, since no in-tree model's output changes.

## Details

**Why the encoder needs the processor.** vLLM V1 runs the encoder of an encoder-decoder model through the multimodal encoder path, so the encoder only sees what the processor packs into multimodal items. Encoder prompts without multimodal data skip the processor, which leaves a text encoder with no input.
- With the flag, `_process_singleton(force_mm_processing=True)` calls `_process_multimodal(prompt_token_ids, {}, ...)` and copies `prompt` and `cache_salt`, as `_process_tokens` does.
- It lives in `_process_singleton` rather than `_process_tokens` because `HfRenderer` overrides `_process_tokens`.
- `_process_enc_dec(_async)` enables it for the encoder prompt only.

**What moved into the plugin** (vllm-t5gemma2-plugin, branch `use-vllm-extension-points`):
- A `ModelState` from `get_model_state_cls()`: Model Runner V2 builds the tower LoRA mapping in the order of `scheduled_encoder_inputs`, while `EncoderDecoderModelState` runs the encoder in batch order. The plugin's state runs the encoder in the mapping's order, and the model moves the cross-attention K/V into batch order after projecting them.
- A `CrossAttention` subclass that passes the plugin's backend to `Attention.__init__`.
- On GPU with Model Runner V2, the plugin's tests pass with these (float16 on FlashAttention, and float32 on its PyTorch attention). With the plugin's state replaced by `EncoderDecoderModelState`, its LoRA test fails again.

**Duplicate check.**
- Open PRs matching "T5Gemma", "text-only encoder" and "encoder-decoder plugin" show nothing that overlaps.
- vllm-project/vllm#32617 (T5Gemma 2 in-tree) was closed after the review asked for a plugin. This PR follows that guidance and keeps the model out of tree.

**AI assistance.** This PR and the plugin were written with AI assistance (Claude Code). The submitter has reviewed every changed line and ran the validation above.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

Thanks @NickLucche! Both work: the plugin now uses its own `ModelState` (via `get_model_state_cls()`) and a `CrossAttention` subclass, and runs on unmodified vLLM, so I reverted those two commits. Details are in the updated description.

For the processor side, the plugin now registers its own renderer (a `t5gemma2` tokenizer mode, like `inkling` and `cohere`) that sends text-only encoder prompts to the processor. @DarkLight1337, is that the kind of plugin control you had in mind? If so, I'll drop the flag and keep only the docs entry. Otherwise the flag would let the plugin use the stock renderer instead of copying `_process_enc_dec`.
Yes, the plugin should control everything if the base behavior needs to be overridden, instead of modifying the in-tree implementation.

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

@Chen-afk-art thanks! Still not sure whether we want to support the changes required by this model, especially the processor side, would be nice if we could allow plugins more control there @DarkLight1337 

To spare the model runner changes instead, could you check if you can define your own ModelState for the model you want to add in the plugin, and see if that allows you to do what you want? (see GemmaDiffusion as an example)
I dont think we need to support this change here, this could live in your plugin where you can define your own attention backend
